newsitem.title: PERU: "Black box" from crashed Boeing found off Peru.
newsitem.headline: "Black box" from crashed Boeing found off Peru.

text.p: Rescuers on Saturday found one of the two "black box" flight recorders and seven corpses from the wreckage of a Boeing 757-200 that crashed 12 days ago off Peru's Pacific coast killing all 70 on board.

An underwater robot made the finds more than 200 meters (475 feet) below the sea, 40 miles (65 km) offshore north-west of Lima in a joint operation by Peru's navy, local airline Aeroperu and U.S. firm Oceaneering Technologies.

The bodies were taken to the morgue at Lima's port of Callao, while the flight recorder was taken for examination by aviation experts investigating the cause of the tragedy, Aeroperu and navy officials said.

The Peruvian government blamed the accident on technical faults that made the computers aboard the plane "go crazy," leaving the pilot, Eric Schreiber, without instruments as he struggled to return through dense fog to Lima after taking off for the Chilean capital of Santiago.
But an investigative team from Boeing, engine maker Pratt & Whitney, the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transporation Safety Board, has reserved judgment.
The 70 dead, including 61 passengers and nine crew members, came from Chile, Peru, Mexico, Ecuador, the United States, Italy, Great Britain, New Zealand, Spain, Colombia and Venezuela.
